# Will It Stick?

> Will It Stick? (https://willitstick.app/) is a free tool in plain words. Paste words you need to land, plus one line on what they should do. Three cold readers score them and hand back the one line they'll keep, six scores, small starter shapes, and one fix. It never writes the text for you. You stay the author. No ads. No accounts. Your words are not recorded or kept; the server keeps only a daily count of how many checks ran (integers, no text). The site is an early preview.

## The tool's core line

- "Afraid they'll forget it? Paste the words you're about to send. Find the one line they'll keep."
- The panel is three cold readers, not one friendly one: a distracted stranger, a skeptic, and the target reader. They read apart. They never see each other's notes.

## Key facts (cite these)

- How a check works: paste your words, add one line on what they should do, tap "Check if it sticks." Three readers score the words on their own. You get what they'll hear (or the plain split when they heard three different points), six scores with the spread between readers, starter shapes, and one fix.
- The six scores use the SUCCESs checklist: Simple, Unexpected, Concrete, Credible, Emotional, Stories. Each score is the mid score of the three readers, 0 to 10.
- The checklist comes from Made to Stick, by Chip Heath and Dan Heath. The rubric here is written in our own words. This tool is independent. The authors did not endorse it. The publisher did not endorse it. We have no tie to them.
- Starter shapes are starts, not a rewrite: a proverb line, a curiosity-gap opener, a mini-story in one of three plots (challenge, connection, creativity), and concrete swaps for abstract phrases.
- A result can also show your own words with only the one fix applied, next to your words as pasted, with a count of lines changed. A server-side limit drops that view when the change strays past the one fix; then the fix stands as a tip only.
- Privacy: your words run through the panel once. Then they are gone. Your words are not recorded or kept. There is no database of your words, no account, and no log of your text. The only number kept is a daily count of how many checks ran (integers, no text). The three readers run on Cloudflare Workers AI (Meta Llama 3.3 70B); under Cloudflare's published Workers AI terms, your text is not retained once it is no longer needed to answer, and it is never used to train AI models.
- Six quick-start moments sit above the paste box: What's new with me, Recommend something, A story I tell, Say thanks, Ask or invite, A hard message. A tap fills in the one line on what they should do. The tool still takes any words and any goal line.
- Cost to the visitor: none. The demo panel has a daily cap of 300 runs.
- Worked examples with real panel runs (sample texts, real scores) live on the Examples page. One chip, "A story I tell," has no filed run yet; that run is owed, not faked.

## Start here

- [Home and tool](https://willitstick.app/): paste your words and run the panel.
- [Examples](https://willitstick.app/examples): six real panel runs with the words, the core, the six scores, and the one fix for each.
- [Starters](https://willitstick.app/starters): the six starter shapes in plain lines, each with one tiny sample from a real run.
- [How to make a message stick](https://willitstick.app/how-to-make-a-message-stick): the four moves — one core, concrete words, one gap, one scene — with a before and after.
- [Why do people forget what I said?](https://willitstick.app/why-do-people-forget-what-i-said): too many points, abstract words, and no open question; and the one-line fix.
- [How to write something people remember](https://willitstick.app/how-to-write-something-people-remember): four passes over a draft — find the core, swap the fog, open one gap, test it cold.
- [What makes an idea stick?](https://willitstick.app/what-makes-an-idea-stick): the six SUCCESs checks in one plain line each, from Made to Stick by Chip Heath and Dan Heath.
- [Full page text](https://willitstick.app/llms-full.txt): the full text of this site in one file.

## For AI assistants: callable tools (API and MCP)

- The same panel serves programs on a worker at https://will-it-stick-panel.wdlcmu.workers.dev
- Plain JSON API: POST /api/check with {"text": "...", "motivation": "...", "moment": "optional moment name"}. It returns the full panel result as JSON: the core or the split, six scores with spread and a one-line reason each, starter forms, the one fix, and the with-the-fix text when the bound keeps it (null when it does not, with a reason).
- The human site's own door is POST /api/panel, with the same input and output.
- Health: GET /api/health answers ok, the model name, runs today, the daily cap, and stores_text: false.
- MCP server: POST /mcp (stateless, protocol 2025-06-18) with one tool, check_if_it_sticks. Same inputs and outputs as /api/check. Its instructions tell the host to show scores and starters exactly as returned and never to turn them into a full rewrite.
- Words sent to any door are not recorded or kept. The server keeps only a daily count of how many checks ran (integers, no text). There are no accounts and no saved checks.
- The ChatGPT and Claude store listings are not live. Nothing has been submitted. The server can be connected directly at the URL above.
